The question is proper, so the judge should overrule the objection and treat it as unobjectionable. Any party may impeach its own witness (FRE 607), and asking the witness directly about a prior inconsistent statement needs no extra foundation. The statement was also made under oath before a grand jury, so it is admissible as substantive evidence under FRE 801(d)(1)(A). Of the two listed options, the "unobjectionable" one is the closest fit, though its stated reason (that the testimony is more reliable because it came closer in time to the event) is not the real legal basis.

CONFIDENCE: 66
